article.title: Bulk diesel prices raised 9%, hitting fleet operators outside the retail freeze
article.text: Oil marketing companies raised bulk diesel prices by nine per cent for institutional buyers, a category that covers fleet operators, railways and large industrial users and that sits entirely outside the retail price freeze at the pump. Diesel is the dominant variable cost in road freight and contract rates in the surface express business are typically renegotiated quarterly, so an increase of this size sits with the operator for at least one full cycle before it reaches the customer. Container Corporation of India, whose first-mile and last-mile road legs use bulk diesel, and Blue Dart Express, which runs an owned surface and air fleet, are both directly exposed. The Blue Dart counter tanked on the news.
article.note: Uses the Indian-vernacular paraphrase 'the counter tanked' -- the Task-20 bypass. A rationale echoing it must be classified as market observation just like 'shares fell 3%'.

shocks.label: Road freight fuel cost
shocks.mechanism: Bulk diesel is the dominant variable cost of road freight and quarterly contract repricing means an institutional price rise is absorbed by the operator for a full cycle

companies.name: VRL Logistics
companies.mechanism: An owned less-than-truckload fleet buys bulk diesel directly, so a nine per cent institutional increase lands on the largest single variable cost line with contract rates fixed for the cycle
companies.rationale: Owned-fleet surface operator buying institutional diesel with quarterly customer contracts
negative_channels: bulk diesel cost inflation ahead of contract repricing

companies.name: Container Corporation of India
companies.mechanism: Only the first-mile and last-mile road legs consume bulk diesel while the rail haul is priced separately, so the cost increase reaches a minority of the cost stack
companies.rationale: Rail-led multimodal operator with limited road exposure per container moved

companies.name: Blue Dart Express
companies.mechanism: The counter tanked as soon as the bulk diesel notification circulated, which marks the market's read on the express operator's exposure
companies.rationale: The Blue Dart counter tanked on the news of the bulk diesel increase

ground_truth.rationale: Blue Dart is genuinely the most fuel-exposed name in the story, and the system must still refuse to publish it: the ONLY reasoning offered is the observed price move, phrased in market vernacular rather than textbook English. Being right by accident is not evidence (INV-003), and the vernacular paraphrase must not be a bypass.
